transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Evan Liu (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Marcus Reed (CTO, Atlas Health), Leah Gomez (Lead ML Eng), Omar Castillo (Platform Eng)

Summary:
Quick sync on POC integration progress. Focus on SDK usage for function/tool calling, structured output stability, and a short run of latency/cost numbers from staging. Open items are Dedicated pricing, staging access, and scenario where KV cache + batching hit edge cases.

Topics covered:
- SDK patterns & client-side retry/backoff
- Function calling and schema enforcement for structured outputs
- Graceful degradation when model variants or quantized variants used
- VPC/staging networking and benchmark plan

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Evan Liu: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:06] Marcus Reed: Marcus here. Leah and Omar are on.
[00:09] Leah Gomez: yep, Leah here.
[00:11] Omar Castillo: Omar, hi.
[00:13] Priya Sharma: Priya from Redwood, hey team.
[00:16] Evan Liu: cool. agenda — short progress updates, show the SDK invoke pattern we recommended, talk about the structured output failures we saw, and then next steps. okay?
[00:25] Marcus Reed: sounds good. we tried the SDK last week, a few things — our microservice that wraps the SDK is getting about 120ms median when calling hosted, but when we push through the staging Dedicated instance the p95 jumps and we saw some KV cache misses.
[00:40] Priya Sharma: okay interesting — is that with batching on? and are you using continuous KV cache or just prefix cache?
[00:46] Leah Gomez: we enabled batching for a subset, but most of the time we keep batch size low because we want tail latency. for caching we tried the SDK's prefix cache option but we think our prefix keys were slightly different across requests, so hit rate low
[01:04] Priya Sharma: yeah that aligns — batching reduces cost but can increase cold p95. one trick is dynamic batch sizing: lower batch window for low-qps endpoints then raise it in peaks. Redwood Optimize will recommend profiles but you can also tune the SDK client side.
[01:18] Omar Castillo: the KV cache behavior worries me — if the service is serving multiple tenants we can't share cache. can we pin to a quantized model variant when cache miss rate high?
[01:27] Priya Sharma: you can pin per-route model version. we also have a lightweight quantized variant for Dedicated that keeps latency low — but note quantized models sometimes produce subtle output diffs, esp. for structured output.
[01:40] Leah Gomez: that's actually what we saw yesterday — schema keys reordered and one enum mapped to a slightly different token, which broke our downstream parser.
[01:49] Evan Liu: right this is a classic tradeoff — cost/latency vs deterministic structured outputs. for the POC acceptance criteria we should pick a model variant family that meets your output fidelity for the function calling path.
[02:01] Marcus Reed: can you walk through the recommended function calling pattern again? our current impl just passes tool definitions as free text.
[02:08] Priya Sharma: sure. recommended: use the SDK's explicit function signature feature — define JSON schema for each tool and set strict mode on the call. SDK will do schema validation and return a normalized object. if schema mismatched it returns a structured error instead of raw text.
[02:26] Leah Gomez: in practice we had the SDK try to auto-cast strings to numbers and that caused silent conversions. is strict mode enforced server-side?
[02:34] Priya Sharma: strict mode is validated by the Redwood runtime. we also provide a 'dry-run' mode for schema validation in the staging environment so you can see rejections without counting tokens.
[02:45] Omar Castillo: nice. about retries — when function call times out we saw double-invokes of downstream systems. is idempotency token guidance in the SDK?
[02:54] Priya Sharma: yes, SDK supports idempotency keys per request. recommend generate a uuid per top-level user action and set that on all retries. plus set exponential backoff in SDK config.
[03:05] Evan Liu: also consider route-level fallback: if the primary model times out, route to a smaller quantized variant for best-effort results — Redwood smart-routing can do that automatically if you set a fallback policy.
[03:18] Marcus Reed: ok on security, Omar flagged SSO and audit logs for the Private deployment. we need to confirm KMS integration and long-term audit retention options.
[03:27] Priya Sharma: KMS is supported — both cloud KMS and customer HSM. audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM via S3 or a streaming connector; retention tiers are configurable — we'll share the SOC2 whitepaper.
[03:39] Leah Gomez: can we get RBAC scoped keys so developers only access staging tokens?
[03:44] Priya Sharma: yep, Workspaces + per-token scopes are standard. we can provision short-lived tokens with limited model access for devs.
[03:51] Omar Castillo: networking — we tried VPC peering but saw higher egress when we routed through a NAT. what's the recommended pattern?
[03:59] Priya Sharma: for Private/Dedicated the recommended is VPC peering with private endpoints; avoid NAT where possible. we can provide a checklist to reduce cross-az egress.
[04:10] Marcus Reed: good. now on the short run numbers — Leah, want to share the staging run summary?
[04:15] Leah Gomez: sure. we ran 15 minutes with 200 rps, function calling enabled, 50% structured outputs. median latency 180ms, p95 620ms, token cost roughly $0.005 per request on that model family. we saw spikes up to 1.2s when cache miss + cold kernels happened.
[04:34] Priya Sharma: couple notes — the staging Dedicated we used had mixed-instance sizing; for predictable p95 you can reserve GPU profile with prewarmed kernels. also kernel warmup is impacted by sequence length distribution.
[04:47] Evan Liu: we observed similar in our lab runs — if you pin sequence length estimates and use KV cache warmups you cut p95 by ~40%.
[04:55] Leah Gomez: question — how do we measure structured-output regressions at scale? we tried random sampling but it's noisy.
[05:02] Priya Sharma: Redwood Console supports eval sets tied to prompt templates. we can automate A/B rollouts and regressions alerts on strict schema mismatches. I can share a template for your acceptance tests.
[05:13] Marcus Reed: that would help. also curious about function chaining — our pipeline has multi-step invokes, and we saw increased cost. any tips?
[05:22] Priya Sharma: optimize by pushing trivial logic client-side or combine multiple function schemas into a single composite call when possible to avoid round trips. batching across steps sometimes helps but watch semantics.
[05:33] Omar Castillo: curious about fallback behavior when a function throws structured error — we want to route to a human-in-loop. is there an easy hook?
[05:40] Priya Sharma: yes, add an onError webhook in the function schema; runtime emits structured error payload and trace id so you can link to the Console trace for quick debugging.
[05:51] Evan Liu: quick demo — Priya, can you share your screen and show the SDK snippet we recommended?
[05:55] [screen share]
[06:02] Priya Sharma: (shows code) const res = await redwoodClient.invoke({ model: 'redwood-llm-s1', route: '/atlas/summary', functions: [schema], strict: true, idempotencyKey: xid }); then check res.functionResult; if error res.error.code === 'SCHEMA_MISMATCH'...
[06:22] Leah Gomez: looks similar to our impl but we missed idempotency. we'll add that.
[06:27] Marcus Reed: about the model name, is 'redwood-llm-s1' the same as the one you'd run in Dedicated?
[06:32] Priya Sharma: it's a family name — there's an s1 quantized variant for Dedicated and an s1-ht for hosted with higher fidelity. we can map those in route config.
[06:44] Omar Castillo: any risks with running function calling + streaming? we have streaming parsers downstream.
[06:50] Priya Sharma: streaming works but structured output with streaming requires delimiting tokens; we recommend using the SDK's chunked structured mode so each chunk is validated incrementally. small chance of partial object at chunk boundary — SDK will provide chunk diagnostics.
[07:05] Leah Gomez: ok good. final open items?
[07:09] Evan Liu: recap: Evan will send Dedicated pricing + commit options; Priya shares benchmark harness and Console eval template; Atlas grants staging network access; Leah finalizes acceptance prompts. we schedule the perf run 2026-10-28.
[07:23] Marcus Reed: fine. any blockers from Atlas side? Omar: networking timeline is the blocker.
[07:29] Omar Castillo: I'm scheduling peering and will try to have creds by 10/23.
[07:33] Leah Gomez: I'll get the prompt set to Priya by 10/24.
[07:36] Evan Liu: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links.
[07:40] Priya Sharma: I'll also drop the SOC2 and KMS notes.
[07:43] Marcus Reed: thanks, bye.
[07:45] Meeting ends.
